question: What are the two main qualities that make a research tool trustworthy?
explanation: Reliability and validity ensure that a research tool measures things consistently and accurately. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is using a well-designed data collection tool so important in midwifery research?

options.A: It ensures findings can safely guide maternal health policies
options.B: It reduces the total cost of conducting field interviews
options.C: It eliminates the need for ethical approval from the hospital
options.D: It guarantees that statistical software will run without errors

explanation: Accurate tools produce trustworthy data, which is essential when research outcomes are used to shape healthcare practices for mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h1)

question: What type of error happens when data is consistently pushed in one direction due to a repeatable bias?
explanation: Systematic errors occur consistently due to flawed tools or procedures, skewing the study results in a specific direction. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h2)

question: A clinic blood pressure cuff reads 10 mmHg too high on every antenatal patient because of a stretched spring. What kind of error is this?
explanation: A constant, predictable shift in every reading caused by a faulty device is an example of a systematic measurement error. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which statistical test is commonly used to check if the questions in a survey hang together well?
explanation: Cronbach's alpha is the standard metric researchers calculate to confirm that items within a scale measure the same underlying concept. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h3)

question: Two midwifery students use the same checklist to grade a student delivery practice and get nearly identical scores. What type of reliability is this?
explanation: When multiple observers use the same tool independently and arrive at similar ratings, it demonstrates strong inter-rater reliability. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which type of validity involves experts reviewing a tool to check if it covers all parts of a topic?
explanation: Content validity relies on experts checking whether the tool comprehensively covers every necessary dimension of the studied topic. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why must a new postpartum depression screening tool be compared against an existing trusted test?

options.C: To reduce the sample size needed for the study
options.D: To eliminate all random measurement errors

explanation: Comparing a new tool directly to a trusted standard proves its criterion-related validity by showing it performs just as accurately. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the relationship between a research tool's reliability and its validity?

options.A: Reliability and validity are completely independent properties
options.B: High validity automatically guarantees high reliability
options.C: An instrument must be invalid if it is reliable
options.D: An instrument can be reliable without being valid

explanation: Consistency does not mean accuracy; a tool can consistently measure the wrong thing, making it reliable yet invalid. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which statement is true about whether an instrument needs to be reliable to be valid?

options.A: Reliability and validity must have identical numerical scores
options.B: An instrument cannot be reliable unless it is first valid
options.C: An instrument cannot be valid unless it is first reliable
options.D: Improving validity always destroys an instrument's reliability

explanation: If a tool gives wildly inconsistent results from day to day, it cannot possibly be measuring the target concept accurately. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason for running a pilot test before starting a research study?

options.A: To collect the final data needed for your primary hypothesis
options.B: To prove that your study has 100% statistical validity
options.C: To identify confusing wording and cultural misunderstandings
options.D: To eliminate all possibilities of systematic measurement error

explanation: A pilot test serves as a dry run to catch unclear questions, formatting issues, or cultural barriers before launching the main study. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is back-translation used when a questionnaire is translated into a local Nigerian language?

options.A: To reduce the number of respondents needed for the sample
options.B: To ensure the clinical meaning has not been distorted
options.C: To comply with international funding agency regulations
options.D: To make the data analysis process faster for statisticians

explanation: Translating back to the original language helps check if the clinical and conceptual meaning survived the initial translation process intact. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h6)
